question: What issues can trust_remote_code introduce, and why does MAX reconstruct configuration objects in a spawned worker?

version_selection.reason: Linux dependency resolution in the checked-out repository; not a claim about every installed runtime or the latest release.
version_selection.other_platform_note: This lock also includes Transformers 5.12.1 for a Darwin dependency group.

upstream_sources.finding: Adds the module cache to the import path, resolves code files and relative imports, registers modules, executes code, and resolves the requested class.
Selects the remote configuration class when the AutoConfig mapping and trust settings permit it; otherwise selects a registered built-in configuration.
Requires review of repository code and recommends fixing the revision when trusting remote code.
Ordinary pickling uses a class module and qualified name. Class definitions must be importable in the receiving environment; instance state is serialized separately from class code.

historical_reports.finding: PicklingError for a custom DeepseekV2Config with a class-identity mismatch.
historical_reports.limits: The report documents the symptom; the synthetic experiment separately demonstrates module replacement as one mechanism. No claim that module replacement is the report's established root cause.

historical_reports.finding: ModuleNotFoundError when a spawned process tries to resolve the transformers_modules package for a repository name containing a dot.
historical_reports.limits: Historical custom-model example; not a MAX or configuration-only reproduction.

historical_reports.finding: Loading a saved model on a new offline machine still attempts to retrieve custom code.
historical_reports.limits: A saved weights/config directory does not prove all referenced custom Python code is available.

historical_reports.finding: ImportError for is_torch_fx_available after an upstream API removal.
historical_reports.limits: A custom-model import example, not evidence that MAX loads that modeling file during AutoConfig reconstruction.

historical_reports.finding: Remote DeepseekV3Config lacks qk_head_dim while the built-in configuration computes it.
historical_reports.limits: The observation applies to the reported model and versions; it is not a general statement that remote configuration fields are always missing.

max_sources.finding: Drops HF and generation config objects and repository handles in copied state; rebuilds them from saved identity during unpickling. No separate GenerationConfig pickling failure is identified.
Maintains an interpreter-local HF config cache and invokes the HF configuration loader.
Uses the spawn context for the model worker.
The saved example uses model_type llama and has no auto_map; this configuration follows the built-in route.

cpu_experiment.scope: Synthetic local DemoConfig in fresh isolated Python interpreters. No HF imports, remote-code execution, model weights, MAX inference or GPU execution.
outcomes: Replacing the parent module class raises PicklingError for an older instance.
Transferring plain source identity and rebuilding succeeds.

interpretation_limits: The demonstrated pickle mechanisms can explain why dynamic objects need special handling; not every dynamic class is unpickleable.
MAX avoids transferring the omitted HF configuration object. Other objects passed to a worker are outside this conclusion.
Reconstruction does not provide repository code, install compatible dependencies, guarantee identical behavior across revisions, or sandbox code execution.
Primary issue reports preserve their reported versions. They are not an assertion of currently unfixed bugs in the inspected Transformers release.

class_identity_followup.question: Does class identity mismatch make API-to-model object transfer impossible? Explain pickle, reload and the reported vLLM error from first principles.
class_identity_followup.source_version: CPython v3.10.12, matching the local experiment runtime

primary_sources.finding: The serializer resolves the class name in the sending interpreter and raises PicklingError if the resolved object is not the class being serialized.
The accelerated serializer implements the same class identity check.
Reload re-executes module code and rebinds names; pre-existing instances continue to use their old class definition.
Ordinary instance pickle stores a class reference and instance state. Unpickling finds the class and restores an instance, usually without calling __init__.

vllm_report_interpretation.observed_boundary: V0 engine creates a tensor-parallel worker; process.start reaches reduction.dump and ForkingPickler.dump before PicklingError.
vllm_report_interpretation.limit: The report establishes the class mismatch, not which earlier operation replaced that class. Reload is an independently demonstrated mechanism, not a claimed root-cause diagnosis of this vLLM report.

cpu_experiment.device: CPU; fresh isolated Python subprocesses and a stdin pipe
outcomes: Ordinary instance pickle is transferred as bytes and successfully unpickled in a fresh worker.
Repeated ordinary import preserves the parent class identity.
An unchanged source file, explicitly reloaded, creates a different class object with the same module and class names.
The old instance keeps its original class and fails parent-side serialization.
A new instance of the currently published class serializes and transfers successfully.
cpu_experiment.limits: Synthetic local DemoConfig only; no Hugging Face/MAX imports, remote code, model weights, GPU execution or reproduction of a model-specific issue.

teaching_boundaries: A, B and C in the diagrams identify class objects, not class-name strings. A and B coexist in the sender; C belongs to the receiver.
The failure check is within the sender. Different object identities in separate processes are expected.
The readable class-reference/state example is conceptual, not the binary pickle format.
The normal and reload diagrams are browser illustrations grounded in the Python run; browser buttons do not execute Python.
MAX still serializes the outer PipelineConfig and MAXModelConfig. Its custom state omits the HF config object and reconstructs that field in the worker.
